title: Echocardiographic findings suggestive of complex mitral valve abnormalities in an adult with ALCAPA: a case report
authors: Dongyang Zhang; Zejie Li; Hexuan Wang; Yafeng Hao
abstract: Background Anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) is a rare congenital coronary anomaly. Previous reports of associated structural mitral abnormalities in adults have predominantly described isolated abnormalities. Case presentation We report a 38-year-old man with adult-type ALCAPA who presented with acute decompensated heart failure. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe mitral regurgitation and complex mitral structural findings, suggesting that ischemia alone might not explain the regurgitation. The patient was initially managed for valvular heart disease. Coronary computed tomography angiography and coronary angiography subsequently confirmed ALCAPA. He declined surgery, and medical treatment relieved his symptoms. At 1-year telephone follow-up, he reported occasional exertional chest tightness and dyspnea but no rehospitalization. Conclusions This case highlights the need to assess both coronary anatomy and mitral valve morphology in adults with ALCAPA and severe mitral regurgitation, as ischemia alone may not fully explain the valve findings. In adults with ALCAPA and complex mitral valve abnormalities, anatomical and functional assessment can clarify the mechanisms of MR and guide concomitant mitral valve surgery. Unexplained heart failure with severe MR and childhood exertional symptoms should raise suspicion of ALCAPA. Preserved LVEF does not exclude reduced forward cardiac output or myocardial injury. Medical therapy may stabilize the patient but cannot replace surgical correction.

title: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacter hormaechei and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from mammary and postoperative wounds in canine oncology patients
authors: Carolina Magri Ferraz; Melrian Menezes Teixeira; Vinicius Bastos Dos Santos; Driele Lutzke; Evelyn Cristine Silva; Karina Gutierrez; Igor Luiz Salardani Senhorello; Fábio Sossai Possebon; Fábio Parra Sellera; João Pedro Rueda Furlan; Gabriel Augusto Marques Rossi
abstract: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales represent an increasing challenge in small animal medicine due to their limited treatment options and potential for dissemination in clinical settings. Although ESBL-positive Enterobacterales are increasingly recognized in dogs, their detection and clinical significance among dogs with cancer remain poorly investigated. Herein, we report the detection and genomic characterization of three ESBL-producing isolates recovered from wound samples of two dogs with neoplastic diseases. One Enterobacter hormaechei isolate was recovered from an ulcerated mammary tumor, whereas another E. hormaechei isolate and a Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate were recovered from a postoperative wound following thoracic nodulectomy. All three isolates were classified as multidrug-resistant and belonged to clinically relevant sequence types: E. hormaechei sequence type (ST) 114 and ST133, and K. pneumoniae ST11. All isolates carried bla CTX−M−15 , while K. pneumoniae ST11 additionally harbored bla CTX−M−8 . Genomic analyses also identified multiple virulence-associated determinants, including siderophore-associated genes in E. hormaechei ST133. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first published report of E. hormaechei ST133 in a dog. These findings highlight the detection of clinically relevant ESBL-producing lineages in canine oncology patients and reinforce the importance of microbiological surveillance and antimicrobial susceptibility testing in veterinary practice.

title: Successful Caesarean Delivery in Severe Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Using Low-Dose Intrathecal Bupivacaine–Fentanyl Technique: Case Report
authors: Mir S. Aaqib; Neesa Waqrul
abstract: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a rare but potentially life-threatening cause of heart failure occurring toward the end of pregnancy or in the early postpartum period. Anaesthetic management of parturients with PPCM poses significant challenges due to markedly reduced cardiac reserve and risk of acute decompensation during delivery. We report the successful anaesthetic management of a parturient with previous lower segment caesarean section and peripartum cardiomyopathy with severe systolic dysfunction (Ejection Fraction 30%) and global hypokinesia who underwent repeat caesarean delivery under low-dose spinal anaesthesia using hyperbaric bupivacaine 7.5 mg and fentanyl 25 mcg. Careful titration of neuraxial blockade allowed haemodynamic stability and favourable maternal and neonatal outcomes.

title: Mitral valve surgery after failed transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: eight-year survival and functional outcomes from two centers
authors: Lilly Ilcheva Burger; Márta Ambrus; Can Keskinaslan; Rasha Boulos; Petar Risteski; I. Tudorache; Nestoras Papadopoulos; Héctor Rodríguez Cetina Biefer; Omer Dzemali
abstract: Background Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is increasingly offered to patients at low and intermediate surgical risk, yet the outcomes of mitral valve surgery after failed TEER remain poorly defined, and long-term data are scarce. Methods We retrospectively analyzed all consecutive patients who underwent mitral valve surgery after failed TEER at two Swiss centers between January 2017 and April 2024. The primary endpoint was Kaplan–Meier survival; secondary endpoints were perioperative complications and changes in New York Heart Association ( N YHA) class, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and mitral regurgitation (MR) grade, assessed by transthoracic echocardiography before discharge after TEER and before surgery. Cause-specific mortality was analyzed with competing-risk methods. Results Thirty-five patients were included (median age 76 years at surgery; primary MR in 29, 82.9%). Most had been discharged after TEER with non-severe MR (23/35, 65.7%) and underwent surgery more than 30 days later (23/35, 65.7%); severe MR was present in 12 patients (34.3%) at discharge after TEER and in 28 (80.0%) before surgery. Median EuroSCORE II rose from 2.9 (1.6–3.8) before TEER to 6.3 (3.7–17.0) before surgery ( p < 0.001). Repair was achieved in 4 patients (11.4%). In-hospital mortality was 2.9%, but morbidity was substantial: pneumonia occurred in 28.6%, renal replacement therapy in 17.1% and tracheostomy in 11.4%, and median hospital stay was 15 days. Kaplan–Meier survival was 91.4%, 72.5% and 59.0% at 1, 3 and 5 years (32, 21 and 12 at risk); the 8-year estimate of 40.2% rests on a single patient at risk and is exploratory. Eight of 14 deaths were cardiac. No surviving patient had severe MR or NYHA class III–IV at one year. Conclusion Mitral valve surgery after failed TEER was performed with low in-hospital mortality but substantial morbidity, and repair was achieved in only one in nine patients. Most patients came to surgery after later deterioration rather than immediate procedural failure. Durability, rather than acute procedural success, should therefore inform the choice of TEER, particularly in younger and lower-risk patients, and surveillance after TEER should extend beyond the index hospitalization.

title: Intracardiac hemodynamics in critical illness: paradigm evolution from mechanistic understanding and standardized assessment to a holographic future
authors: Xiaoya Cui; Xiaoting Wang
abstract: Hemodynamic disorders in critical illness extend beyond simple “hypotension” or “low cardiac output.” They reflect decompensation of the cardiovascular system driven by the HOUR (Host/Organ Unregulated Response). In critical illness, the heart is not merely an isolated pump; it is also a central target and effector organ directly affected by systemic stress. This review summarizes advances in intracardiac hemodynamic assessment in critically ill patients. First, we describe hemodynamic mechanisms within the HOUR framework and emphasize the need to shift cardiac assessment from reliance on macroscopic parameters toward the study of intracardiac hemodynamics. Second, we discuss the methodological core, the “Intracardiac Hemodynamics 10-Step Assessment Process (10 s-ICEe),” which uses ten standardized steps to provide a systematic, closed-loop evaluation of the physiological pathway from venous return and transvalvular blood flow to arterial ejection. This process provides a practical link between mechanistic understanding and bedside decision-making in the ICU. Third, we examine how emerging technologies, including VFM, HyperDoppler, echoPIV, and 4D Flow MRI, are advancing assessment beyond one-dimensional velocity measurements toward multidimensional analysis of intracardiac vortices, energy loss, and blood flow vectors. We also consider the potential of “holographic cardiac assessment” to integrate structural, functional, blood flow, and perfusion information. This review aims to establish a comprehensive system for assessing intracardiac hemodynamics in critical illness, spanning basic assessment, advanced technologies, and integrated interpretation. It outlines the rationale and pathway for shifting hemodynamic management from structural observation to functional optimization, and from reliance on single parameters to system-level integration.

title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge versus surgical repair in primary degenerative mitral regurgitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Mateo Londoño Barrientos; Juan Fernando Molano Rivera; David Amarillo Gutierrez; Samuel García Vallejo; Juan C. Araque; Luis Andrés Vélez
abstract: To compare transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) with surgical mitral valve repair in adults with primary degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Ovid MEDLINE, Scopus and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to 23 October 2025 (PROSPERO CRD420251153452). The primary analysis included studies of DMR with a surgical repair comparator; cohorts with a predominantly replacement comparator and administrative registries entered separate sensitivity analyses. Odds ratios (OR) were pooled with the Mantel–Haenszel method, with random-effects models as sensitivity analyses. Certainty was rated with GRADE. Nine studies were included; five (775 patients) formed the primary analysis. TEER was associated with more residual mitral regurgitation of at least moderate grade (OR 8.21, 95% CI 4.56–14.79) and more mitral reinterventions (OR 4.10, 1.69–9.94), and with fewer transfusions (OR 0.11, 0.05–0.23), less new-onset atrial fibrillation (OR 0.09, 0.03–0.28) and a shorter hospital stay (random-effects mean difference −3.6 days, −6.2 to −1.0). Early mortality did not differ significantly (OR 2.03, 0.62–6.61; 12 deaths), but the interval was too wide to establish equivalence. Four of the five primary studies ended enrolment before 2018. Certainty was low to very low. Surgical repair remains the reference treatment for patients with favourable operative risk and repairable anatomy. TEER is a valuable alternative for carefully selected patients in whom procedural safety or surgical risk predominates, at the cost of less complete and less durable correction. The absence of a significant difference in early mortality does not demonstrate equivalence.

title: Case Report: Aortic valve Haemophilus parainfluenzae infective endocarditis complicated by a fistulating aortic root abscess and refractory atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response
authors: Korah Shalan; August Lynch
abstract: This report details the case of a gentleman in his 50s, with a background of previous bicuspid aortic valve infective endocarditis 28 years prior, presenting to hospital with non-specific symptoms, including shivers, headaches and myalgia. Objective clinical findings included pyrexia, hypotension and atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response (AF RVR). He was initially provided with empirical intravenous antibiotics and isotonic fluids to treat an infection of unclear origin. Despite equivocal preliminary imaging findings, blood cultures isolated Haemophilus parainfluenzae , an organism implicating endocarditis, and his antibiotics were switched to Ceftriaxone. Even with this change in antibiotics, he consistently remained febrile, developed a significant Troponin-I leak, and his AF RVR exceeded 200 bpm – unamenable to pharmacological rate and rhythm control therapy. Transoesophageal echocardiography later confirmed an aortic root abscess fistulating into his left ventricular outlet tract, where the patient thereupon underwent an aortic valve replacement with patch reconstruction. Post-procedure, his AF was now responsive to Amiodarone, successfully restoring sinus rhythm. His inflammatory markers additionally improved before he was discharged home to complete his four-week Ceftriaxone course under the virtual ward – achieving a successful outcome. Especially in patients with overt risk factors, this case reinforces the need to maintain a high index of suspicion for infective endocarditis in patients presenting to the acute medicine with pyrexia of unknown origin. This case was, however, also remarkable for capturing significant AF RVR instead of the anticipated heart blocks with abscess formation and serves to emphasise the heterogeneity of Haemophilus parainfluenzae endocarditis cases.

title: Segmental Anaesthesia for Cesarean Section in a Patient with Severe Dilated Cardiomyopathy and Twin Pregnancy: A Case Report
authors: Rajesh Kumar; Richa Tripathi
abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) during pregnancy is associated with significant maternal and fetal morbidity due to reduced cardiac reserve and the risk of haemodynamic decompensation. Anaesthetic management becomes particularly challenging in the presence of severe left ventricular dysfunction and twin gestation, as these conditions may further compromise cardiac function and become life-threatening. We report the successful anaesthetic management of a 43-year-old primigravida at 34 weeks of gestation with dichorionic diamniotic (DCDA) twins and severe DCM (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] 28%) undergoing elective caesarean section. Low-dose segmental spinal anaesthesia combined with epidural anaesthesia was employed to achieve controlled sympathetic blockade and maintain haemodynamic stability. With invasive monitoring, inotropic support, and meticulous perioperative care, a favourable outcome was achieved. This case highlights the importance of regional anaesthesia in managing high-risk cardiac parturients.

title: Intracranial Subdural Empyema Associated with Streptococcus Dysgalactiae Subsp. Equisimilis in a Patient with Chronic Subdural Hematomas
authors: Ryo Yonai; Ryota Sato; Takashi Shinzato
abstract: A 73-year-old man with conservatively managed bilateral chronic subdural hematomas presented with fever and vomiting, followed by a seizure and impaired consciousness. Craniotomy revealed subdural pus, supporting intracranial subdural empyema arising in these hematomas. Streptococcus dysgalactiae subsp. equisimilis (SDSE) was recovered from blood and subdural cultures, although a polymicrobial infection could not be excluded because subdural sampling followed antibiotic initiation. He improved after drainage and four weeks of antibiotic treatment. SDSE bacteremia with neurological deterioration should prompt consideration of subdural empyema. Hematogenous seeding was considered to be the most likely route of infection.

title: Combined Mitral and Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: Evidence, Patient Selection, and Procedural Strategy
authors: Georgios  E Papadopoulos; Vlasis N. Ninios; Ilias Ninios; Sotirios Evangelou; Apostolia Marvaki; Maria Kalaitzoglou; Andreas Ioannides; Andrew V. Xanthopoulos; John S. Skoularigis; Grigorios Giamouzis
abstract: Concomitant mitral regurgitation (MR) and tricuspid regurgitation (TR) constitute an interconnected multivalvular syndrome, but correction of MR does not consistently reverse TR. This narrative review examines TR evolution after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), patient selection, imaging, procedural strategies, and evidence for treatment of both valves. Combined TEER denotes bivalvular treatment, performed during the same session or in stages. Observational cohorts report TR improvement in approximately one-third of broadly selected patients after M-TEER, with substantial variation according to baseline severity, response definition, and follow-up. Persistent or new-onset TR is associated with adverse outcomes; these associations do not establish that subsequent tricuspid intervention improves survival. Comparative registries suggest potential clinical benefit from combined treatment, whereas uncontrolled series primarily establish technical feasibility in selected patients at experienced centers. Treatment timing remains uncertain because randomized comparisons of isolated, same-session, and staged strategies are unavailable. The proposed Heart Team framework integrates lesion-specific indications, anatomical suitability, anticipated TR reversibility, physiological reserve, and patient goals. It is an unvalidated discussion aid rather than a treatment recommendation. Randomized strategy trials are needed to establish incremental clinical benefit, comparative safety, and optimal timing.

title: Mapping the Cell-Cell Interactions in Cardiovascular Diseases: A Single-Cell Atlas Perspective
authors: Seungyoon Song; Cherin Lee; Park Hun-Jun; Jae‐Joong Kim
abstract: Cell-cell interactions play a critical role in maintaining cardiovascular homeostasis by coordinating communication among cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells, and immune cells. In cardiovascular disease (CVD), these interactions become dysregulated, driving inflammation, fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, and adverse remodeling. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have enabled the construction of detailed cellular atlases of the human heart and vasculature, allowing systematic inference of intercellular communication through ligand-receptor analysis. These efforts have uncovered disease-specific alterations in key signaling pathways. In this review, we summarize the major changes in intercellular communication observed across diverse cardiovascular pathologies. We highlight how altered crosstalk among vascular, stromal, and immune cells contributes to cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction and heart failure. Understanding these disrupted signaling networks provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms of CVD and may guide the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring healthy cell-cell communication.

title: University performance in cardiovascular research: A TOPSIS-based bibliometric analysis of highly cited publications
authors: Maryam Tavanarezaei; Mobin Golabzaei
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide, driving substantial research investment and necessitating robust evaluation of institutional research performance. This study employed the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) to evaluate and rank the research performance of 30 leading universities based on their contributions to the top 100 highly cited cardiovascular medicine articles from 2010–2026, extracted from Scopus. Three evaluation criteria were selected: Unique Authors (minimized as a resource input measure), Total Citations (maximized as an impact indicator), and Number of Papers (maximized as a productivity measure), with equal weights (33.3% each) assigned to all criteria. TOPSIS analysis revealed substantial variation in institutional performance, with Harvard University emerging as the top-performing institution (TOPSIS score: 0.6050), demonstrating dominance across all criteria with 228 unique authors, 9,430 citations, and 83 papers, followed by Cleveland Clinic (0.4882), University of Toronto (0.4537), and Mayo Clinic (0.4158). US institutions dominated the ranking, accounting for 27 of 30 universities with an average TOPSIS score of 0.4112, while Canadian institutions achieved an average of 0.4078. The analysis identified an “efficiency gap” between high-citation, low-paper institutions (e.g., UCSF with 87.4 citations per paper and 1.3 authors per paper) and those demonstrating the inverse pattern. The findings highlight the dominance of US institutions, varying institutional strategies (high-volume vs. high-impact approaches), and the concentration of research activity among leading academic medical centers, with the TOPSIS methodology offering a robust framework for multidimensional research evaluation that can inform institutional benchmarking, strategic planning, and resource allocation in cardiovascular medicine.

title: 3D bioprinting of tissues and organs for systemic diseases and localized injuries
authors: W. Kee Ng; Paulo Bártolo
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting integrates engineering, materials science, and biology to fabricate living tissues with precise spatial control. By enabling the layer-by-layer deposition of cells and biomaterials, it overcomes many limitations of traditional scaffold-based tissue engineering and offers new opportunities for regenerative and personalized medicine. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in 3D bioprinting. It introduces a systematic, ASTM-aligned classification of key bioprinting modalities, extrusion, jetting, and vat photopolymerization, along with their respective material and biological design requirements. It also summarizes recent progress in bio-ink development and crosslinking strategies that improve print fidelity and functional tissue maturation. In addition, the review highlights applications in both systemic disease modelling and treatment (such as cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic, and neurodegenerative disorders) and localized tissue repair (including skin, musculoskeletal, cartilage, and bone), emphasizing their relevance to civilian healthcare and military medicine. By combining technological innovation, biological insights, and regulatory considerations, this review outlines how advances in multi-modal bioprinting and intelligent process control can accelerate the translation of laboratory research into clinically viable, patient-specific therapies, driving the next generation of regenerative medicine.

title: LPC-based efficient compression of phonocardiogram signals for IoT-enabled cardiac monitoring systems
authors: Samer J. Alabed; Mohammad Al-Rabayah; Omar M. Bwaliez
journal: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
abstract: This study proposes an efficient linear predictive coding (LPC)-based compression method for phonocardiogram (PCG) signals targeting real-time cardiac monitoring applications. The proposed approach models each PCG frame using LPC to capture its spectral characteristics and represents the remaining information through a residual signal. An adaptive thresholding parameter is applied to the residual to adjust the compression level. By varying this parameter, the proposed framework provides a flexible compression ratio (CR) ranging from approximately 4:1 to 30:1, while maintaining good reconstruction quality and preserving the essential morphology and characteristics of the PCG waveform. The LPC parameters and non-zero residual components are quantized and transmitted to enable signal reconstruction at the decoder. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach can substantially reduce the amount of transmitted PCG data while maintaining high-quality reconstructed signals. The proposed framework therefore provides a computationally efficient and flexible low-bitrate solution for resource-constrained biomedical and remote cardiac monitoring applications.

title: Trial architecture in contemporary cardio-oncology: Why parallel-group randomized controlled trials may not fit every cardiotoxicity phenotype
authors: Radhia Chems Telli
abstract: Cardio-oncology has evolved rapidly with immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, and targeted kinase inhibitors, yet cardiovascular prevention strategies remain largely informed by evidence generated during the anthracycline era. This critical narrative review examines why cardioprotection trials have failed to keep pace with these evolving toxicity mechanisms, analyzing trial populations, endpoint selection, biomarker strategies, imaging approaches, and overall trial design across traditional and newer cancer therapies, rather than summarizing therapeutic efficacy. The evidence shows a persistent mismatch between contemporary toxicity phenotypes and existing trial design: Most studies continue to focus on anthracycline-associated left ventricular dysfunction and surrogate imaging endpoints, while immune-mediated myocarditis, cytokine release syndrome-related cardiomyopathy, vascular toxicities, arrhythmias, and other emerging phenotypes remain inadequately represented, compounded by limited biological stratification, one-size-fits-all prevention strategies, heterogeneous outcome definitions, and insufficient mechanism-specific monitoring. Progress in cardio-oncology prevention is constrained not only by the availability of candidate cardioprotective interventions but by the near-uniform persistence of a single trial architecture across mechanistically distinct toxicities. Future studies should adopt phenotype-driven, mechanism-informed, adaptive trial designs using clinically meaningful outcomes that reflect the diversity of contemporary cardiovascular toxicities.

title: Cardiac comorbidity role in the diagnosis of diabetes mellitus using single lead electrocardiogram utilizing machine learning model
authors: Anna Dmitrievna Karbovskaya; Basheer Abdullah Marzoog; Snezhana Nikolaevna Demchuk; Anastasia Stroeva; Daniil Andreevich Zelenov; Peter Chomakhidze; Natalia Kuznetsova; Syrkin Abromavich; Valentin V Fadeev; Irina V. Poluboyarinova; Sevindzh M Ismailova; Philipp Kopylov
abstract: BACKGROUND Cardiovascular disease alters electrocardiographic morphology and may obscure diabetes-related electrical signatures, yet its effect on electrocardiogram (ECG)-based detection of type 1 and type 2 diabetes is poorly defined. AIM To investigate whether cardiac comorbidity differentially influences machine-learning detection of the two diabetes types from single-lead ECG. METHODS In this study, 2591 observations remained after exclusion of an erroneous age entry and rerunning the analytical pipeline. Twenty-six XGBoost models were evaluated separately for type 1 and type 2 diabetes within subgroups defined by seven cardiac-status criteria. Primary models used 47 single-lead ECG features and five anthropometric variables and were evaluated with five-fold stratified cross-validation. A post hoc seven-predictor sensitivity analysis assessed model complexity. Area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC) uncertainty was estimated using 2000 bootstrap resamples of out-of-fold predictions, and ΔAUC comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Calibration was assessed using Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, reliability plots, and decision-curve analysis. Validation was observation-level because a persistent patient identifier was not available in the analytical export. RESULTS After correction and full rerun, median AUC was 0.693 for type 1 diabetes (range: 0.660-0.804) and 0.661 for type 2 diabetes (range: 0.543-0.716). No cardiac-pathology ΔAUC comparison remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment; the smallest adjusted P value was 0.064. In the reduced seven-predictor sensitivity analysis, AUC was higher than the 52-predictor model in 17 of 26 evaluable subgroup models, with a median descriptive difference of +0.008. Calibration was suboptimal: Across the 26 models, calibration slopes ranged from 0.078 to 0.467 and intercepts from -1.287 to -0.535. Decision-curve analysis showed threshold-dependent net benefit rather than uniform superiority across the evaluated range. CONCLUSION Single-lead ECG combined with anthropometric information showed moderate internal discrimination for recorded diabetes status, but the corrected analysis did not identify a cardiac-pathology subgroup effect that remained significant after multiplicity adjustment. The reduced-feature sensitivity analysis suggested that similar discrimination may be achievable with fewer predictors, whereas calibration remained inadequate for direct interpretation of model outputs as disease probabilities. These findings do not establish a clinically validated screening or rule-out threshold. Patient-grouped validation, independent threshold validation, and external validation remain necessary before clinical implementation.

title: Sex effect of E-liquid constituents on atherosclerosis and gut dysbiosis in ApoE−/− mice
authors: Ann Marie Centner; Gwoncheol Park; Leila Khalili; Vladimir Ukhanov; Saurabh Kadyan; Hyun Seok Hwang; Ravinder Nagpal; Gloria Salazar
abstract: Rationale The role of sex in the effects of vaping and individual aerosolized e-liquid constituents on atherosclerosis, vascular aging, and gut microbiome remodeling remains poorly characterized. Objective To determine the contribution of e-cigarette aerosol components to vascular senescence, atherosclerosis, and gut microbiome dysbiosis in ApoE -/- mice and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) viability and senescence. Methods Male and female ApoE -/- mice were exposed to e-liquid constituents (vehicle, vehicle plus nicotine, and vehicle plus nicotine plus menthol) for 48 minutes per day, 5 days per week for 16 weeks, with vascular pathology assessed in vivo. VSMCs isolated from aortas of wild-type and ApoE -/- male and female mice were exposed to aerosolized e-liquids and evaluated for cellular senescence. Results Exposure to all tested e-liquid formulations, including vehicle, nicotine-containing, and menthol-containing aerosols, increased atherosclerosis in both male and female mice, with the most robust effects observed in the nicotine-containing formulation and in the descending aorta. Females exhibited greater sensitivity to e-liquid exposure, with increased plaque accumulation in both the aortic arch and descending aorta, while the addition of menthol was associated with reduced plaque burden compared with nicotine alone in both sexes. Novel findings show that e-liquid exposure also altered gut microbial composition in a sex- and exposure-dependent manner, with nicotine causing the greatest dysbiosis and menthol exerting modulatory, but not restorative, effects. Notably, Alloprevotella emerged as a key discriminating genus associated with reduced plaque burden, supporting a potential link between gut microbial remodeling, inflammatory regulation, and atherosclerosis. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that individual e-liquid aerosol components increase atherosclerosis and alter the gut microbiome in a sex-specific manner, with nicotine producing the most pronounced pro-atherogenic effects and the addition of menthol reducing these effects, without eliminating overall atherosclerotic risk.

title: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT in cardiac Anderson–Fabry disease: novel insights into disease assessment from a case series
authors: Inês Fortuna; Paula Soeiro; Helena Moreira; Teresa Faria; Janete Santos; Mariana Vasconcelos; Catarina Marques; Ana Oliveira; João Paulo Oliveira; Elisabete Martins
abstract: Anderson-Fabry disease (AFD) is an X-linked lysosomal disorder in which cardiac involvement is the main cause of morbidity and mortality, manifesting as left ventricular hypertrophy, heart failure, arrhythmias, and myocardial fibrosis. Myocardial fibrosis is a key pathophysiological process associated with an adverse prognosis. While cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) identifies established myocardial fibrosis, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET enables the molecular assessment of FAP-associated activity. By complementing conventional CMR parameters, including late gadolinium enhancement and native T1 mapping, FAPI PET may improve the characterization and phenotypic classification of cardiac involvement in Anderson-Fabry disease. We report three cases of AFD patients, who underwent Gallium-68-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (⁶⁸Ga-FAPI) PET-CT as part of a prospective study designed to assess myocardial fibrosis. Overall, ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI uptake closely correlated with CMR findings, reinforcing the role of cardiac fibroblast activation as a relevant pathogenic mechanism in AFD. These findings highlight this new molecular imaging as a promising tool for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic guidance in AFD.

title: Association between metabolic obesity phenotypes and cardiac structural and functional characteristics in hospitalized middle-aged and older adults: a single-center retrospective study
authors: Xiuhong Zhang; Tong Chen; Hongjian Jia; Wenhui Zhou; Jietao Zhang
abstract: Objective To examine associations between metabolic obesity phenotypes and echocardiographic structural and functional parameters in hospitalized middle-aged and older adults. Methods Middle-aged and older inpatients who had undergone echocardiographic examination at the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University were retrospectively enrolled. According to BMI and metabolic status, the participants were classified into six groups: MHNW, MHOW, MHO, MUNW, MUOW, and MUO. With the MHNW group as the reference, multiple linear regression and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate the associations between different metabolic obesity phenotypes and echocardiographic parameters. Trend analyses were also conducted across BMI categories within metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy groups. Results A total of 1,320 participants were included: 301 in the MHNW group, 266 in the MHOW group, 65 in the MHO group, 197 in the MUNW group, 326 in the MUOW group, and 165 in the MUO group. Multiple linear regression showed that, compared with the MHNW group, LAD was greater in the other five phenotypes, while LVIDs, IVSd, LVPWd, and LVM were greater in all non-reference groups. LVIDd was greater in all groups except the MUNW group. Multivariable logistic regression showed that the MUOW group had higher odds of elevated RWT, E/A < 1, and abnormal left ventricular geometry. The MUO group had higher odds of E/A < 1. Trend analysis showed that increasing BMI category was associated with greater LAD, RA, RV, and LVIDs, higher odds of elevated RWT and abnormal left ventricular geometry, and lower odds of elevated LVMI in the metabolically healthy group. In the metabolically unhealthy group, increasing BMI category was associated with greater LAD, RV, and LVIDs, as well as higher odds of PASP >35 mmHg (all P-FDR < 0.05). Conclusion Cardiac structural and functional characteristics differed across metabolic obesity phenotypes in hospitalized middle-aged and older adults. The MUOW phenotype showed more consistent associations with elevated RWT and abnormal left ventricular geometry. These findings provide complementary evidence of associations between metabolic obesity phenotypes and selected echocardiographic parameters in an inpatient population.

title: A Case of Hypertrophic Obstructive Cardiomyopathy Posted for Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
authors: Anirban Brahma Adhikary; Jyoti Suthar; Gupta Subodh; Sushmita Adapa
abstract: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) is an autosomal dominant inherited condition in which the interventricular septum undergoes asymmetrical hypertrophy, obstructing the left ventricular outflow tract during ventricular systole.1 The disease can present at any time during lifetime, with patients complaining of dyspnea of various grades depending on the severity of obstruction. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is one of the most commonly performed elective surgical procedures. Patients with gallstone disease get immense benefit from the procedure in terms of relief of signs and symptoms, as well as possible complications of prolonged disease.Patients with HOCM, whose signs and symptoms are well controlled on regular medication, can undergo laparoscopic/open cholecystectomy safely with appropriate anaesthetic and surgical management, and they should not be denied the benefits of undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to their cardiac condition.

title: Material Retention and Infection Persistence in Endocarditis: A Testable Extracellular Hypothesis
authors: Christiano Gondim Moreira
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This conceptual research note examines whether fibrin-rich extracellular material contributes to infection persistence and whether pre-existing valve changes influence susceptibility to infective endocarditis. Drawing on the Temporal Matrix Principle (TMP) and Microenvironmental Metric Engineering (MME), it outlines comparisons to assess whether material changes persist after the initiating disturbance has subsided and whether those changes influence later biological responses. The note considers sterile fibrin–platelet deposits associated with valve injury and distinguishes them from the clinical syndrome of non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis. It also examines rheumatic heart disease as a clinical context for asking whether extracellular changes retained after valvular inflammation subsides alter local mechanics or favor sterile fibrin–platelet deposition during a subsequent challenge. Recurrent inflammation and existing structural damage are considered as alternative explanations. The note presents testable hypotheses based on published literature. It reports no original experimental data. Whether modifying matrix turnover can limit scarring while preserving valve function and normal growth, especially in children, remains a question for preclinical research.

title: Clinical Reference Values for Left Ventricular Diastolic Indices in Stable Outpatients with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction Running Title: Diastolic Reference Values in HfrEF
authors: Ataolla Eskandari; Maryam Chenaghlou; Kamran Mohammadi; Mahdi Karimi
abstract: Background and Aim: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) requires precise assessment of left ventricular filling pressures (LVFP) for optimal management. While guidelines provide thresholds for detecting elevated LVFP, specific reference values for guiding hemodynamic targets in stable outpatients remain undefined. This study aimed to establish clinical reference values for echocardiographic diastolic indices in stable HFrEF patients. Methods This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2023 at the Cardiovascular Research Center of Tabriz University of Medical Sciences. A total of 102 outpatient HFrEF patients (ejection fraction ≤ 40%, NYHA functional class I/II) and 100 healthy individuals with normal cardiac function (ejection fraction ≥ 55%) were enrolled. Patients with significant valvular disease, atrial fibrillation, advanced pulmonary disease, or severe renal failure (eGFR < 30 mL/min) were excluded. Diastolic indices, including left atrial volume index (LAVI), tricuspid regurgitation gradient (TRG), E/e′ ratio, and E/A ratio, were measured using transthoracic echocardiography. Data were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney test in SPSS version 22 (significance level P < 0.05). Results Mean diastolic indices in HFrEF patients were LAVI: 32.5 mL/m² (vs. 25 mL/m² in controls), TRG: 21.5 mmHg (vs. 16.5 mmHg), and E/e′: 12 (vs. 7), all significantly higher than the control group (P < 0.0001). The E/A ratio (0.95 in patients vs. 0.8 in controls) showed no significant difference (P = 0.171). Conclusion The diastolic indices LAVI (32.5 mL/m²), TRG (21.5 mmHg), and E/e′ (12) can serve as clinical reference points for optimizing medical treatment in ambulatory HFrEF patients and for guiding clinical decision-making, as these patients may require drug adjustment to prevent pulmonary congestion and hospital readmissions. Further research is needed to validate these findings and assess their impact on long-term outcomes.

title: Body Form and Architectural Elements for Conservation-Led Daylight Optimization in Cultural Museum: A Case Study of Ikom, Cross River State, Nigeria
authors: Charles Bassey Ephraim; Eugene Ehimatie Atamewan
abstract: Daylight is a valued architectural resource in museum design, yet uncontrolled daylight exposes cultural artifacts to fading, embrittlement, colour change, ultraviolet degradation, glare, and thermal stress.This exploratory article examines how the body form and architectural elements of a cultural museum in Ikom, Cross River State, Nigeria, can optimize daylight while protecting light-sensitive artifacts. Using an exploratory, mixed-methods, design-based approach, and the study integrates literature review, climate and site analysis, cultural heritage assessment, case-study review, and daylight-performance simulation. The article proposes a “Sheltered Grove of Memory” concept: a compact, clustered museum form in which bright public and circulation spaces are separated from low-light, conservation-controlled galleries. The proposed strategy uses deep-plan gallery cores, shaded courtyards, high-level clerestories, roof monitors, light wells, external shading fins, light shelves, diffusing ceilings, ultraviolet-filtered glazing, and automated shading. Conservation thresholds guide the design: a maximum of approximately 50 lux for highly sensitive artifacts, 150–200 lux for moderately sensitive artifacts, and up to 300 lux for durable materials such as stone, ceramic, and metal. The study argues that successful tropical museum daylighting depends not on maximizing transparency but on controlling luminous contrast, solar exposure, and cumulative light dosage

title: Schulen im digitalen Wandel: Stand und Entwicklungen in der Schweiz
authors: Franziska Aeschlimann; Tugsad Akgül; Chiara Antonietti; Tobias Berner; Mireille Bétrancourt; Hana Bida; Stéphanie Boéchat-Heer; Ingo Karl Bosse; Josef Buchner; Eliane Burri; Christiane Caneva; Alberto Cattaneo; Tessa Consoli; Tino Endres; Andrea B. Erzinger; Désirée Delia Diana Fahrni; Michael Geiss; Barbara Getto; Philipp Gonon; Maria Görlich; Christoph Gütersloh; Jessica M. E. Herzing; Ramona Hürlimann; Anna Janka; Sebastian Jansen; Melanie Kieber; Judit Martínez Moreno; Dominik Petko; Doreen Prasse; Caroline Pulfrey; Tobias Röhl; Nadine Scheller; Thomas Schmalfeldt; Christa Schmid-Meier; Marie-Luisa Schmitz; Sascha Schneider; Sabine Seufert; Leonie Sibley; Denise Sutter Widmer; Cécile Vassaux; Mandana York
abstract: Nur wenn Politik und Verwaltung wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse einbeziehen, lässt sich der digitale Wandel im Bildungswesen sinnvoll gestalten. Der Sammelband bündelt aktuelle empirische Erkenntnisse zu dieser Herausforderung. Er bietet einen Überblick über die Folgen der digitalen Transformation von Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft für die öffentliche Bildung in der Schweiz. Die Beiträge basieren auf empirischer Forschung und machen deren Erkenntnisse für Wissenschaft, Politik, Verwaltung und Praxis zugänglich.

title: Short-form video and microlearning in English language education: A bibliometric and science mapping review
authors: Thi My Linh Tran; Huy Hoang Doan
journal: Journal of Pedagogical Sociology and Psychology
abstract: Short-form video platforms, particularly TikTok, have altered how second language learners encounter and process linguistic input. Individual studies have examined specific aspects of microlearning in second language contexts, yet, to the authors' knowledge, no bibliometric analysis has mapped the intellectual structure of this emerging subfield. This study maps the publication landscape, thematic clusters, and research gaps characterizing microlearning research in English language education through short-form video platforms. We conducted a hybrid bibliometric analysis of 80 Scopus-indexed documents published between 2004 and 2026. Performance analysis was performed using Biblioshiny (R), and science mapping was executed through VOSviewer. The bibliometric outputs were then interpreted through a qualitative synthesis using the Theory, Context, Characteristics, and Methodology framework. Three principal patterns emerged. First, scholars from developing Asian economies, including Malaysia, Hong Kong, China, and Indonesia, contributed the largest share of publications, whereas traditional Western academic centers produced comparatively fewer studies. Second, the thematic clusters concentrated on phonological production and vocabulary acquisition, with limited attention to academic writing or reading comprehension. Third, qualitative and experimental designs together accounted for approximately two-thirds of the corpus, while computational learning analytics appeared only peripherally in the keyword co-occurrence network. This bibliometric review maps the knowledge structure of a rapidly expanding subfield at the intersection of educational technology and applied linguistics. The findings point to a need for longitudinal experimental designs, methodological diversification toward learning analytics, and empirical investigation of how algorithmic recommendation systems mediate L2 input delivery.

title: Risk committees and corporate disclosure: Evidence on risk and sustainability reporting with governance moderation
authors: Ria Karina; Teddy Jurnali; Sheila Septiany; Meififanny Taniono
journal: Risk Governance and Control Financial Markets & Institutions
abstract: Environmental and social concerns related to sustainability can represent non-financial risks requiring effective risk management (Wong, 2014). In this context, risk committees may play a role in overseeing such risks and their related corporate disclosures. This study investigates how risk committees impact both risk and sustainability disclosure, aiming to understand how corporate governance enhances transparency and investor confidence. It also examines whether board size, independence, and institutional ownership moderate these relationships, influencing the effectiveness of risk committees in corporate reporting. Using a quantitative approach, this study analyzed 807 samples from Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) companies that published sustainability reports between 2019 and 2023. The results show that risk committees positively influence risk disclosure but do not significantly affect sustainability disclosure. Moderation analysis indicates that board size and independence weaken the effect on risk disclosure. Conversely, institutional ownership strengthens the impact on sustainability disclosure, but not on risk disclosure. These findings suggest risk committees are more effective for traditional risk reporting than for sustainability transparency. This study provides new insights by testing the effectiveness of risk committees in enhancing both types of disclosures. It offers practical insights for regulators, investors, and corporate leaders, underscoring the importance of risk committees in improving disclosure quality to foster transparency and trust.

title: Real-Time Water Quality Forecasting Using a Simulation-Driven IoT and Machine Learning Framework for Resource-Constrained Smart Cities
authors: Belinda Mutunhu Ndlovu
abstract: This study proposes and evaluates a simulation-driven Internet of Things (IoT) and machine-learning framework for real-time water-quality monitoring and forecasting in resource-constrained smart cities. Ensuring timely and reliable water-quality data remains a critical challenge, as conventional monitoring approaches are often delayed, infrastructure-intensive, and difficult to scale. While IoT-based systems support continuous environmental monitoring, many existing implementations emphasise data acquisition rather than predictive analytics and deployment-oriented design. To address this gap, the study develops a unified simulation-based modelling framework in which virtual sensors generate key water-quality parameters, including pH, turbidity, temperature, and dissolved oxygen. The generated data are processed using a machine learning pipeline and used to train supervised models, namely XGBoost, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbours. Model performance is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to ensure balanced assessment across water-quality conditions. The results show that XGBoost achieves the highest predictive performance (91% accuracy), demonstrating strong capability in modelling non-linear environmental patterns and detecting unsafe water conditions. In addition to predictive performance, the framework supports real-time forecasting and visualisation through an integrated dashboard, enabling continuous monitoring and data-driven decision-making. The study contributes a reproducible and scalable framework that integrates simulation-based modelling, IoT-enabled monitoring, and machine learning for predictive analytics. The proposed approach provides a cost-effective pathway for advancing sustainable water management and environmental monitoring in resource-constrained smart-city environments.

title: Future VLSI Architectures for Neuromorphic Computing, Edge AI and Sustainable Systems
authors: R Bhaskar Nihal Varma
journal: International Journal for Multidimensional Research Perspectives
abstract: The future of Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) architectures is being fundamentally reshaped by the intersecting demands of Neuromorphic computing, edge artificial intelligence (AI), and sustainable electronic systems. As traditional CMOS scaling nears its physical limitations, researchers are exploring bio-inspired Neuromorphic designs that mimic the brain's energy-efficient computing mechanisms using spiking neural networks (SNNs), as demonstrated by platforms like Intel’s Loihi and IBM’s True North (Davies et al., 2018; Merolla et al., 2014). In parallel, edge AI is driving the need for VLSI systems capable of performing high-speed, low-latency inference directly on-device, thus reducing reliance on cloud infrastructure. Hardware accelerators such as Eyeriss and Google’s EdgeTPU offer promising solutions through energy-aware architecture and domain-specific design (Chen et al., 2019; Jouppi et al., 2017). These innovations are increasingly evaluated not just on performance, but also on ecological impact. Emerging sustainable VLSI solutions include non-volatile memory technologies like ReRAM and PCM, in memory computing approaches that reduce data movement, and eco-friendly materials like carbon nanotubes and organic semiconductors (Sebastian et al., 2020; Rajendran et al., 2020). However, despite significant advancements, challenges persist in fabrication scalability, algorithm-hardware co-design, and lifecycle sustainability assessment. This paper explores the synergetic evolution of these domains and highlights the critical need for interdisciplinary collaboration to develop future VLSI architectures that are intelligent, efficient, and environmentally responsible. The convergence of Neuromorphic computing, edge AI, and green hardware marks a paradigm shift, positioning VLSI not only as a medium for computation but as a cornerstone of sustainable technological progress.

title: Nasal in-situ Transferosomes as a Platform Technology for Nose-to-Brain Drug Delivery
authors: Dhanush .; D Shripathy; Aradhana Pinto; Sourav Kulal; AR. Shabaraya
journal: Galore International Journal of Health Sciences and Research
abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major obstacle in the therapeutic management of disorders related to the central nervous system (CNS), blocking the access of almost 98% of small molecule medications and practically all large molecules. Intranasal drug administration represents a viable alternative to overcome the BBB, based on its ability to deliver directly from the nasal cavities into the brain using the routes of olfactory and trigeminal nerves, offering a direct nose-to-brain drug delivery pathway. Despite its advantages, intranasal drug delivery remains constrained by factors such as quick clearance, short retention and poor permeation of the drugs through biological membranes, to address these challenges, the in-situ gelling systems containing mucoadhesive polymers have been developed. Nasal in-situ transferosomal gels offer a novel formulation technique that incorporates the benefits of both transferosomal vesicular drug delivery systems and stimuli-responsive gel matrices for brain targeting. Keywords: Transferosomes, in-situ gel, Intranasal, Nose-to-brain, Blood-brain barrier, Vesicular drug delivery, Mucoadhesive systems, Brain targeting.

title: Sinkhole susceptibility and genesis at the southwestern slope of the Mount Sirino (Basilicata, Southern Italy): insights from field survey and machine learning modeling
authors: Patrizio Petricca; Stefania Nisio; Pantaleone De Vita; Giancarlo Ciotoli; Vincenzo Allocca
journal: Rendiconti online della Società Geologica Italiana
abstract: The southwestern slope of the Mount Sirino (Basilicata, Southern Italy) is characterized by complex geological conditions favouring heterogeneous sinkhole phenomena. The most prominent geomorphological feature is Lake Sirino, formed on a large landslide deposit and frequently affected by piping-related sinkhole phenomena. This study uses an integrated approach combining geological and geomorphological surveys, remote sensing and machine learning modelling to investigate the genetic mechanisms of sinkhole formation at Lake Sirino and its surrounding areas (c. 100 km²). Fieldwork identified ten natural sinkholes, mainly associated with deep-seated piping processes in detrital deposits overlying low-permeability substrate. The Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) algorithm was used to create a susceptibility map of natural sinkholes in the study area. This analysis identified lithology and fault density as the primary predisposing factors. The results highlight that sinkholes development in the Lake Sirino area is controlled by the interaction between high hydraulic gradients, fractured zones, and contrasting permeability layers.

title: “Calcare Cavernoso” as a key predisposing factor for sinkhole occurrence in Tuscany (Italy): inventory update, remote sensing detection, and GIS–ML susceptibility modelling
authors: Marina Funaro; Stefania Nisio; Sergio Madonna
journal: Rendiconti online della Società Geologica Italiana
abstract: The “Calcare Cavernoso” (cavernous limestone) formation is a dolomitic carbonate unit characterized by a vacuolar texture and high intrinsic porosity, which favours groundwater-driven dissolution and cavity development and may predispose to subsidence. This study investigates the spatial relationship between sinkholes and the distribution of “Calcare Cavernoso” in Tuscany (Italy) and updates the regional subset of the ISPRA national sinkhole database. An integrated approach combined bibliographic information, targeted field surveys, historical cartography, and multi-source geospatial datasets. Geological and thematic layers were retrieved from the Tuscany “Geoscopio” portal, while Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery was processed using the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) to support the detection of flooded sinkholes. Historical maps were exploited to infer sinkhole persistence and potential evolutionary trends, including partial or complete infilling. All thematic layers (geology, faults, hydrography, quarries, mines, topography, and sinkholes) were harmonized, georeferenced, and rasterized on a 250 × 250 m grid within an ESRI ArcGIS environment. Susceptibility modelling was implemented using density-based proxies and an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) framework, producing probability outputs subsequently grouped into classes to enhance operational usability. The results substantially expand the regional sinkhole inventory (from 88 to 1223 mapped features) and support a strong spatial association between sinkhole occurrence and “Calcare Cavernoso”, further corroborated by targeted field checks. The most influential susceptibility drivers include “Calcare Cavernoso”, low-slope settings, DTM-derived parameters, fault density, and anthropogenic underground activities (quarries and mines), while other variables show secondary or more complex contributions.

title: Anthropogenic sinkholes in the urban fabric of Messina (Sicily, Italy)
authors: Mauro Bonasera; Stefania Nisio; Luigi Guerriero
journal: Rendiconti online della Società Geologica Italiana
abstract: Urban anthropogenic sinkholes are increasingly reported in Messina (Sicily, Italy), where culverted torrents, legacy underground works, and dense utilities intersect a Holocene coastal/alluvial plain. We present an updated, georeferenced inventory of sinkholes within the municipal urban area, built from local press/ web sources and field cross-checks, and we assess spatial relationships with culverted drainage and known urban cavity entrances. To frame site-effects in a seismic setting, we consult the Italian catalogue of earthquake-induced ground failures (CEDIT) and the Italian catalogue of earthquake environmental effects (EEE), which document widespread ground cracking, settlement and liquefaction during major historical earthquakes, notably the 1908 Messina event. Our results highlight clusters along culverted stream corridors and in zones influenced by underground legacy, supporting future scenario-based prioritization of inspections and post-event checks.

title: Mapping natural sinkhole susceptibility in Italy: integrating a national inventory with machine learning
authors: Livio Ruggiero; Giancarlo Ciotoli; Federico Mori; Sergio Madonna; Stefania Nisio
journal: Rendiconti online della Società Geologica Italiana
abstract: Natural sinkholes are a widespread geohazard in Italy, complicating landuse planning and risk reduction. This study develops the first national-scale susceptibility map for natural sinkholes using an updated inventory and data-driven modelling. Building on the ISPRA National Sinkhole Database, we assembled more than 14,000 documented features from literature, historical records, imagery and regional datasets. Geological, geomorphological, structural, hydrogeological and geochemical factors were converted into gridded predictors and combined with the inventory through a machine-learning regression framework estimating a continuous susceptibility score. The calibrated model, evaluated on a held-out 20% test subset, produces a susceptibility surface for the Italian territory. Interpretation tools emphasize the importance of soluble rocks, fault-controlled permeability, deep gas emissions and mineralized springs, consistent with previous studies. High-susceptibility zones align with major karst and evaporitic provinces, including the Friuli-Veneto piedmont, northern Apulia, Latium travertine basins and central Sicilian evaporites, whereas western Alpine sectors and Sardinia show very low scores. The map offers a coherent national overview of where natural sinkholes are more likely to occur and provides an operational basis for prioritizing surveys, monitoring programmes and planning measures, while the methodology can be refined to incorporate time-dependent drivers and multi-hazard interactions. These advances support more resilient and sustainable territorial development.

title: Educational architecture as cultural space: structuralist influences in the work of Hestnes Ferreira
authors: Alexandra Saraiva; Jorge Amaral
journal: Cidades, comunidades e território/Cidades comunidades e territórios
abstract: This article explores the cultural and architectural significance of the José Gomes Ferreira Secondary School (JGFSS) in Lisbon, designed by Raúl Hestnes Ferreira, through the lens of Dutch structuralism and the humanist theories of Herman Hertzberger. More than an educational facility, the school is conceived as a civic and cultural microcosm: an adaptable urban fabric that fosters community interaction, symbolic meaning, and spatial versatility. Drawing on key structuralist principles such as Hertzberger’s “architecture as a half-product,” Aldo van Eyck’s polyvalent space, and John Habraken’s “Supports” theory, the study situates the school within a broader European discourse on architecture’s social role. It also reflects on Ferreira’s formative 1974 study trip to Scandinavia, which reinforced his commitment to human-centred design and spatial openness. The article aims to examine how structuralist principles informed the design of the José Gomes Ferreira Secondary School, to analyse the influence of Hestnes Ferreira’s engagement with Scandinavian educational architecture, and to assess how adaptability, modularity, and social space contribute to the school’s role as a cultural and socially sustainable environment. This study adopts a qualitative case study methodology, combining archival research, analysis of architectural drawings, photographic documentation, and interpretation of interviews and recorded lectures by the architect. The research is grounded in a theoretical framework based on structuralist and humanist architectural theories. The findings highlight the school’s enduring relevance as a model of culturally engaged architecture, where modularity, symbolism, and social adaptability converge to create a space that transcends its educational function and contributes to the cultural identity of its community.

title: Common Edible Mollusks Sold in the Local Markets in the Municipalities of Capiz, Philippines
authors: Stephanie S. Pimentel
abstract: This study aims to determine the identity, availability, diversity, marketability, coastal sources, merchandise, and commercial value of different edible mollusks sold in the local public markets in the province of Capiz. Information on the various edible mollusks sold in Capiz's local public markets was gathered through interviews with vendors who participated as respondents. The survey, conducted from June to August 2024, involved thirty-nine (39) vendors from different local markets. During the interviews, vendors were shown pictures of the mollusks to ensure clarity and consistency in identifying the species, which may have different local names across locations. The most frequently sold edible mollusks in Capiz's local markets are Perna viridis (Asian green mussel) and Magallana bilineata (Philippine cupped oyster), available in all markets, with a majority of vendors selling them. On the other hand, less commonly sold species include Tegillarca granosa (blood cockle), Anodontia edentula (toothless clam), Bractechlamys vexillum (distant scallop), and Dolomena turturella (dog conch), which are sold in fewer local markets and by fewer vendors. Out of the nineteen species in the study, Perna viridis (tahong) was identified as the fastest-selling edible mollusk, while Telescopium telescopium (bagongon) was the slowest-selling. Magallana bilineata (talaba) ranked second among fast-selling mollusks and third among slow-selling ones. Marcia hiantina (punaw), Antigona lacerata (tuway), Telescopium telescopium (bagongon), and Modiolus philippinarum (abahong) were observed to be both fast-selling and slow-selling in various local markets within the province. The speed of sale appears to correlate with market demand, with high-demand species being sold quickly and those with lower demand moving more slowly. This may also be true for other coastal commodities in the province. This study reveals production and other relevant data on the merchandise, commercialization, distribution, and source availability of edible mollusks in the province.

title: Evaluating Digital Technologies’ Economic and Environmental Effects on Compliance, Governance, and Privacy in Sustainable Environmental Management
authors: Nathan Udoinyang
abstract: The purpose of the study was to analyze new technologies impact on environment. The prospective benefits and challenges of new technologies on the use of technologies within environmental governance and compliance were uncovered in this study. Utilizing a convergence approach of qualitative and quantitative studies, the researchers sent out a survey to 9407 stakeholders within the environment, which included civil society, the private sector, and government. The study found out that the enforcement and reporting of compliance with environmental legislation would be greatly assisted by the streamlining of governance and compliance in the adoption of new technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT), The study also acknowledged the presence of other challenges such as inadequate infrastructure, expensive technologies, and poor technical capacity. The gaps and challenges on the governance of the environment, compliance, and sustainability would be solved by the introduced new technologies, which in turn would create a sustainable environment. This would lead to the development of Nigeria in an economically sustainable manner, while also providing overall environmental sustainability. The paper recommend that Nigeria's should increase her investment in the construction of training facilities within the administrative regulatory systems of new technological systems in environmental sustainability, collaborative Joint ventures should be encouraged so as to achieve economies and environmental sustainability.

title: Graphene-Derived Nanomaterials for Wastewater Treatment: Bridging Laboratory Performance and Practical Feasibility
authors: Sonali Bhatt
abstract: Rapid industrialization and urbanization have increased the discharge of complex pollutants into aquatic systems, posing significant environmental and public health challenges. Conventional wastewater treatment technologies often fail to remove trace contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, heavy metals, and emerging organic compounds. Graphene-based materials, including graphene oxide, reduced graphene oxide, and graphene quantum dots, have emerged as promising candidates due to their high surface area, tunable surface chemistry, mechanical robustness, and unique electronic properties, enabling diverse removal mechanisms such as adsorption, catalysis, and membrane filtration. Laboratory studies have shown that these materials can achieve superior pollutant removal efficiencies; however, their large-scale implementation remains limited, highlighting the gap between laboratory performance and industrial feasibility.This review provides a structured assessment of graphene-based materials for wastewater treatment. Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature review covering 2010–2024 was conducted, with emphasis on the latest 2025 studies addressing techno-economic and industrial feasibility. The review examines the types of graphene materials, their physicochemical properties, and functionalization strategies, followed by critical evaluation of their applications in removing various contaminants. Key research gaps, including aggregation, fouling, regeneration loss, toxicity, and lack of standardized protocols, are discussed. The techno-economic and industrial feasibility section analyzes production costs, scalability, energy requirements, and lifecycle considerations. Finally, future perspectives on AI-guided material design, smart membranes, and regulatory frameworks are outlined to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and practical development.

The aim of this research is to explore the influence of electronic training (ET) on job satisfaction (JS) as well as job performance (JP) among employees in the banking sector.Furthermore, it aims to determine whether JS mediates the relationship between ET and JP.Data were gathered using a survey distributed to a sample of 320 employees working in Jordanian banks.The current study relied on the structural equation modeling (SEM) approach, with AMOS as the selected software for data analysis.The findings indicate a direct positive effect of (ET) on (JS) (β = 0.547) and (JP) (β = 0.587).Furthermore, a positive association exists between (JS) and (JP) (β = 0.349).An important finding of this research is the recognition of ET and JS as factors that influence JP.The current research responds to existing gaps in the previous literature regarding the influence of electronic training on job performance and the mediating function of job satisfaction among them.

title: Autism s Paradoxical Nature: Understanding Contradictory Characteristics
authors: Sinan Kalkan; Fatma Erdoğan
journal: Kalem Uluslararasi Egitim ve Insan Bilimleri Dergisi
abstract: Autism-specific traits and the behaviours associated with them often give rise to dilemmas that can be conceptualized as paradoxes. These paradoxical patterns are characterized by the coexistence of marked cognitive or social challenges alongside unusual or exceptional abilities within the same individual. Such dualities highlight the complexity and heterogeneity of autism and underscore the need for integrative conceptual frameworks. Positioned as a conceptual theoretical discussion, this article draws on literature from neuroscience, developmental psychology, education, and philosophy to reconceptualize autism through the organizing lens of paradox. Drawing on theoretical perspectives such as Kapur’s “Paradoxical Brain” framework, the review illustrates how functional neurodevelopmental imbalances may simultaneously contribute to both strengths and limitations across developmental domains. Rather than providing a purely descriptive overview, this review integrates existing literature to identify recurring paradoxical patterns in autism and examines their implications for daily life, diagnostic practices, and individualized intervention strategies. Understanding the paradoxical dimensions of autism is essential for moving beyond deficit-oriented models, optimizing individual strengths, and developing more inclusive and responsive support systems. By highlighting both individual and societal implications, this theoretical discussion aims to contribute to a more nuanced understanding of autistic experiences and capacities and to inform future research and practice.

title: Analysis of Influencing Factors and Effects of Biochar on the Adsorption of Pollutants in Water
authors: Hongyan Chen; Li-Juan Feng; Jinhong Zhang; Jinyu Luo; Wenlin Li
abstract: This research article delves into the factors influencing the adsorption of pollutants in water using biochar. The study investigates the physical and chemical properties of biochar, its interaction with various pollutants, and the environmental conditions affecting its efficacy. Through a series of experiments, the adsorption capacity of biochar is quantified, and the results are analyzed to understand the underlying mechanisms. The findings contribute to the development of more efficient water purification systems using biochar as a sustainable material.
